title: Client Echo Notebook — probe plays and request hypotheses
content:
Purpose: quick synthesis of recent customer threads (Feb–Mar 2029), surfaced asks, and small probe ideas we can ship as low-effort mitigations or test hypotheses with product/eng. This is intentionally rough — cribnotes for triage and rapid experiments.

Top-level summary (1–2 lines each):
- Reliability friction: three customers reported sudden increase in tail latency when using long-context chat (1000+ tokens) concurrently with embedding backfills. Suspect KV cache eviction + burst batching policy mismatch.
- Cost sensitivity: two mid-market customers want clearer per-route per-model cost estimates pre-launch (not just historical billing). They want a way to simulate cost for expected QPS + average token lengths.
- Private deployment onboarding gap: security teams flag gap in HSM/KMS documentation for air-gapped installs; they ask for a checklist + example terraform snippets.
- Determinism/regressions: a customer noticed different output distributions after switching to a new quantized variant (x4bit). They want a rollback path and quality checks in console.

Customer vignettes (short):
1) AlphaHealth (enterprise, healthcare) — Impact: blocking for pilot. Behavior: when clinicians use long multi-turn summaries, latency spikes 2–3x and some replies truncation. Linked ticket: CS-3421. Notes: running Dedicated, GPU pool pinned to A100-80GB. Current mitigation implemented: reduced max_tokens on client side (temporary). Need: a graceful fallback policy and knob to favor latency over throughput per route.
2) FinEdge (growth-SaaS) — Impact: planning friction. Ask: pre-launch cost simulator to estimate monthly inference spend for multiple traffic scenarios. Wants CSV upload of sample prompts. Benefit: reduces procurement friction for Dedicated. Linked artifact: Slack thread Mar 9 2029.
3) RetailCo (mid-market) — Impact: security review delay. Ask: concrete KMS/HSM example and audit log retention SLA for Private. Will not proceed to pilot without this.

Observed signal clusters (evidence):
- Latency cluster: CS-3421, CS-3498, field notes from March 12 (3 customers). Common pattern: long prefix + concurrent embedding jobs.
- Cost visibility cluster: multiple sales calls, one inbound trial cancellation flagged cost unpredictability.
- Private onboarding docs: 2 legal/security review blockers in last 6 weeks.

Immediate probe plays (quick experiments to run in 2–4 weeks):
A) Burst policy probe: enable conservative burst cap for routes tagged "interactive-long" for 2 weeks on Dedicated accounts exhibiting spikes. Measure P50/P95/P99 pre/post. Owner: Samir. JIRA: CS-3489 (investigation).
B) Cost-sim CSV upload prototype: small UI mock + lambda that runs cost heuristic against sample prompts (simulate token distribution x QPS). Deliverable: clickable demo for sales. Owner: Alyssa. Success metric: reduces procurement questions in pilot calls by 40%.
C) Private docs mini-package: 1-pager + terraform snippets + audit log checklist. Owner: Meera. Target: reduce security hold time by 2 weeks for new pilots.
D) Quantized variant rollback path: add quick toggle in Console to fall back to float32 variant and capture evaluation metrics on the offending prompt set. Owner: Eng-sre liaison. Quick metric: time-to-fallback < 3min.

Low-effort UX fixes (can ship in sprints):
- Add a "simulate cost" button on route creation that opens a modal and accepts simple parameters (QPS, avg tokens, retention period).
- Surface model variant lineage in Console (which commit/quantization profile applied); show a "known regressions" badge if there are alerts.
- Add a canned troubleshooting checklist for "long-context tail latency" in support docs and link to it in the incident creation flow.

Prioritization rationale (quick):
- Burst policy probe (A) = high impact, low dev cost (config toggle + monitoring) — move to top of backlog.
- Cost simulator demo (B) = high sales enablement value, medium effort — prioritize for coming sprint for sales collateral.
- Private docs (C) = low engineering cost, high impact on closed deals — urgent for enterprise CS.
- UX/rollback (D) = medium cost, high reliability value — schedule after A/B.

Open questions & unknowns (needs eng/product):
- Do we have telemetry hooks to distinguish KV-cache eviction vs. batching backpressure? (SRE input needed)
- For the cost simulator: do we simulate quantization impacts on token cost (latency) or only per-token pricing?
- Can we offer a documented "latency first" runtime profile that preconfigures batching and cache TTLs per route?

Proposed next steps (for CS + product sync):
1) Triage meeting Fri Mar 29 — review telemetry and scope burst policy toggle. (Attendees: CS lead, eng-sre, product-hosted-api).
2) Samir to run initial telemetry query for affected customers by Mar 26. Deliver: P95 traces + KV cache eviction counts.
3) Alyssa to build cost-sim clickthrough prototype and share in sales demo by Apr 5.
4) Meera to assemble Private docs mini-package and request legal review.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Samir Gupta: telemetry slice for CS-3421/CS-3498 (due 2029-03-26).
- Alyssa Chen: cost-sim prototype + sales demo (due 2029-04-05).
- Meera Patel: Private deployment checklist draft + TF snippets (due 2029-03-28).
- Jamal Ortiz: draft support checklist article for long-context latency (due 2029-03-27).

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could we expose a "dry-run billing export" that produces a monthly cost CSV for a route, using the customer's expected token histogram? Useful for procurement.
- Consider a "pilot-friendly" package: 30-day reduced retention + pre-wired fallback policies + cost-sim for new Dedicated pilots to speed time-to-first-success.
- Add a prompt-level quality check in Console: before rollout, run a small eval of X sample prompts across model variants and show delta in hallucination/score.

Appendix — quick logs & references:
- CS-3421: customer-reported tail latency on long-context chat, posted Mar 10 2029. Slack thread: #customer-alphahealth.
- CS-3489: burst policy investigation ticket (internal).
- GH PR 1983: batching policy change (notes: landed Feb 14 — could correlate).

If you are reviewing: please add quick notes inline, mark items you own with initials, and flag anything that should be escalated to product leadership.

—— end cribnotes ——
